CausalChain: Iron overload in liver -> Excess labile iron fuels Fenton reaction -> Elevated ROS production increases mitochondrial lipid peroxidation -> Impaired mitoNEET function exacerbates mitochondrial iron dysregulation -> Amplified lipid peroxidation compromises GPX4 (and system Xc⁻ activity) triggering ferroptosis -> Hepatocyte death intensifies liver injury -> Enhanced mitoNEET function plus upregulated system Xc⁻/GPX4 axis restores iron-homeostasis, reduces ROS and lipid peroxidation, and prevents ferroptosis
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that hepatocyte-specific dual precision gene therapy—achieved via optimized viral vectors and CRISPR-based transcriptional activation—simultaneously enhancing mitoNEET (CISD1) activity and upregulating the system Xc⁻ component will restore mitochondrial iron equilibrium by lowering the labile iron pool and curtailing the Fenton reaction. This, in turn, reduces ROS-driven mitochondrial lipid peroxidation and preserves the function of GPX4 by ensuring adequate glutathione synthesis. By directly addressing both the source of iron-mediated oxidative damage and reinforcing the antioxidant defense, this combined approach aims to prevent ferroptotic cell death and ultimately ameliorate liver injury associated with iron overload.
Abstract: We propose a refined therapeutic strategy against iron overload–induced liver injury that couples precision genetic activation of mitoNEET (CISD1) with concurrent upregulation of the system Xc⁻/GPX4 axis in hepatocytes. Leveraging state‐of‐the‐art gene delivery systems and CRISPR-based transcriptional activators, our approach aims to restore mitochondrial iron homeostasis by reducing the labile iron pool that feeds the Fenton reaction. In parallel, by enhancing glutathione biosynthesis through system Xc⁻ upregulation, the preserved GPX4 function further limits ROS-dependent lipid peroxidation. The combined intervention is designed to mitigate ferroptotic cell death, counterbalance compensatory autophagic responses, and ultimately ameliorate liver injury associated with iron overload. This dual-modality strategy acknowledges both the direct modulation of mitochondrial iron handling via mitoNEET and ancillary antioxidant pathway reinforcement as critical elements in the cascade leading from iron overload to hepatocyte death.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis focused solely on enhancing mitoNEET function to reduce the labile iron pool, thereby decreasing ROS-driven lipid peroxidation and preventing ferroptosis. The revised hypothesis retains this core causal chain—starting from iron overload to ROS generation via the Fenton reaction and subsequent lipid peroxidation—but now integrates a dual intervention strategy that also upregulates system Xc⁻ for improved glutathione synthesis and GPX4 preservation. Additionally, the new approach leverages contemporary gene delivery and CRISPR-based techniques to ensure precise, hepatocyte-specific activation, while explicitly addressing potential compensatory mechanisms (e.g., autophagy) that may also influence redox balance and ferroptosis prevention.
